name: Infantile Neurodegeneration-Progressive Spasticity-Intellectual Disability-White Matter Lesions Syndrome
aliases: Infantile Neurodegenerative Disorder with Spasticity and White Matter Lesions

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for Infantile Neurodegeneration-Progressive Spasticity-Intellectual Disability-White Matter Lesions Syndrome

criteria.description: Progressive spasticity beginning in infancy or early childhood
Developmental delay or intellectual disability manifesting in infancy
MRI evidence of diffuse or multifocal white matter lesions
Clinical and/or radiological evidence of progressive neurodegeneration
Exclusion of metabolic or infectious causes of white matter disease

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: progressive spasticity, intellectual disability, and white matter lesions on MRI
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other leukodystrophies and metabolic disorders.

pathognomonic.notes: Typically begins in infancy and worsens over time
searchTerms: increasing stiffness and weakness in legs
tightness and difficulty moving lower limbs

pathognomonic.symptomName: Diffuse cerebral white matter lesions on MRI
searchTerms: brain MRI showing white matter damage

pathognomonic.symptomName: Global developmental delay with intellectual disability
pathognomonic.notes: Manifests within first two years of life
searchTerms: global developmental delay with intellectual disability
slow growth in skills and cognition

common.notes: Speech difficulties due to motor impairment

occasional.notes: Visual impairment secondary to nerve degeneration
Poor sucking and swallowing in infancy
Joint contractures due to chronic spasticity
Including difficulty initiating or maintaining sleep

rare.notes: Sensory deficits reported in isolated cases
Mild liver enlargement in rare presentations

laboratory: Exclusion of metabolic leukodystrophies by enzymatic assays
imaging: MRI showing diffuse or multifocal white matter hyperintensities on T2-weighted images
Progressive cerebral atrophy in advanced stages
genetic: No specific gene identified; suspected autosomal recessive inheritance pattern
other: Electroencephalogram (EEG) may show nonspecific slowing or epileptiform activity

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of metachromatic granules in nerve biopsies
Later onset compared to infantile neurodegeneration syndrome
Elevated N-acetylaspartic acid in urine and brain

redFlags: Rapidly progressive spasticity with loss of acquired milestones
MRI showing extensive white matter lesions without metabolic cause
references: Orphanet: Infantile Neurodegeneration-Progressive Spasticity-Intellectual Disability-White Matter Lesions Syndrome, ORPHA:641353
Neurogenetics Journal, 2023: Clinical and Imaging Features of Infantile Neurodegeneration Syndromes
